name: Orion ExchangeWithOrionPool depositAsset reentrancy
summary: Exchange.depositAsset() carries no reentrancy guard and credits the caller with the exchange's own token balance delta, while swapThroughOrionPool() settles a caller-supplied token path by crediting the balance delta of the path's output token. The attacker put a fake ERC-20 in the middle of the path whose transfer hook re-entered depositAsset() with flash-loaned USDT, so the same 2.84M USDT was credited twice and withdrawn once.
notes: Eleventh and last pre-exploit Upgraded event of the exchange proxy, emitted by ProxyAdmin 0xee913f6f0016db2929a0b2061a38f1461ef93477 calling upgrade(); it selected implementation 0x98a877bb507f19eb43130b688f522a13885cf604, which the EIP-1967 implementation slot still holds at block 16542147.

Net USDT movement of the exchange 0xb5599f568d3f3e6113b286d010d2bca40a7745aa in the exploit receipt: it receives 2,844,766.426326 USDT from the attacker contract through the re-entrant depositAsset call plus 0.000099 USDT from the OrionPool pair, and pays out 5,689,532.852749 USDT in the closing withdraw, for a net loss of 2,844,766.426324 USDT. The 0.4999 USDC the attacker deposited to open the position is an attacker input and is not netted. This record is scoped to the Ethereum leg only. The same defect was executed against the Orion exchange on BNB Chain 0xe9d1d2a27458378dd6c6f0b2c390807aed2217ca in transaction 0xfb153c572e304093023b4f9694ef39135b6ed5b2515453173e81ec02df2e2104 for a further 191,606.635567209086337063 BSC-USDT; no incident record exists for that chain, so it is excluded here rather than folded into this Ethereum measurement. Reported campaign totals near USD 2.9M are the sum of both legs. DefiLlama's nearest USDT observation to the incident timestamp is 1.0031 at 1675353310; par valuation is used, which is 0.31 percent conservative.
